name: Kurmin Dangana
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020. Research on the Plateau languages of Central Nigeria. Afrika und Übersee 93: 3-44. doi:10.15460/auue.2020.93.1.209 (the 'Blench 2020 pp. 19-22' cited by Glottolog)
sources.note: Hyamic section p. 21: 'Apart from Hyam of Kwoi, these languages remain very poorly known (see Jockers 1982)'; 'It now seems likely that the Hyam cluster consists of only Hyam of Nok, Sait, Dzar, while Yaat and the language of Ankun are also probably distinct, although proof is lacking.' Kurmin Dangana not named; no 'stress'/'accent' anywhere in the article.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2019/2020. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, edition IV
sources.note: 'Kurmin Dangana' occurs once, as a member of the Hyamic list in the Plateau classification (p. 109); no headword entry, no references. 'Yaat' listed separately as 'member of Hyam cluster'. The Hyam entry cites only wordlists Gerhardt (1988, 1992), Blench (2012, 2014) and grammar Jockers (1982).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. n.d. [page dated 2012]. Hyamic page, rogerblench.info (Wayback captures 2015-04-21 and 2025-05-27) and directory index of /Language/Niger-Congo/BC/Plateau/Hyamic/ (server listing 16 Jun 2012)
sources.note: Table lists Hyam of Nok, Shang, Cori, Kurmin Dangana; only Hyam of Nok and Shang have linked documents. Folder index and Wayback CDX of the whole Plateau/ tree (1381 rows) show no Kurmin Dangana file and no Hyamic overview PDF ever archived. 2025 capture is garbage bytes (domain lapsed).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2018. Nominal affixes and number marking in the Plateau languages of Central Nigeria. In Watters (ed.), East Benue-Congo, 107-172. Language Science Press.
sources.note: grep Dangana/Yagi = 0; Hyamic treated only via Hyam; no stress statement.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2010 [printout 31 Aug 2010]. A wordlist of the Hyam language of Nok in Central Nigeria and its affinities. Draft, KWEF Cambridge, 31 pp.; and Blench 2006 'You couldn't make it up': the phonology of Hyam (13 pp.)
sources.note: Wordlist sec. 2.2 lists Kurmin Dangana only as one of the settlements where Hyam of Nok is spoken; no separate data. The Hyam phonology (sec. 3.3 Tones: three level tones plus rising/falling) has no stress statement even for Hyam, and nothing on Kurmin Dangana.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2009 [rev. VI, 27 May 2009]. Recent research on the Plateau languages of Central Nigeria. Submitted for the Hamburg Gerhardt retirement proceedings. 23 pp.
sources.note: grep Dangana/Yagi/stress = 0 hits; does not treat this language.

sources.citation: Hayab (John), Philip. 2016. Basic Hyam Grammar with Ethnographic Notes. Abuja: Beltina Digital Press. ISBN 978-978-95298-9-6
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Only modern grammar in the Hyamic group; names Yat = Kurmin Dangana (pp. xiii, 6, 8, 81 per Wikipedia) and may say whether it is a Hyam dialect; the Hyam Literacy site by the same author names 'stress' as an orthography topic. Would supersede Blench's drafts for Hyam and possibly comment on Kurmin Dangana.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2012. The Hyamic languages: A language cluster in Central Nigeria. Draft manuscript, 30 Nov 2012, 15 pp. (Glottolog ref 311120; hhtype overview;comparative;wordlist; 'Yagi = Kurmin Dangana')
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Glottolog's most-extensive description for kurm1245 (2 pp. on the language); the only document known to contain Kurmin Dangana data. Held in Hammarström's hh file; never on Blench's website per Wayback folder index and CDX. A comparative wordlist is unlikely to state a stress rule, but it would settle whether any phonological notes exist.
